Focus on the AdaCoM workflow, the managed-context recurrence, the action space for structured context modification, and the reinforcement learning setup. In the experiments, prioritize comparisons against vanilla ReAct and fixed summarization, the learned context-length or compression behavior, and the transfer matrix across agents. The most relevant part for foundation-model researchers is the Fidelity–Reliability trade-off, because it connects long-context degradation to model capability and suggests why a single context-management heuristic is unlikely to fit all agents.

recommendation.zh: 重点看第5节的Fidelity-Reliability Trade-off实验结论，对长上下文Agent的后训练与策略设计有实际参考价值
recommendation.en: Focus on the Fidelity-Reliability Trade-off results in Section 5, which has practical reference value for post-training and strategy design of long-context agents

institutions: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

paper.title: S3Mem: Structured Spatiotemporal Scene-Event Memory for Long-Horizon Interactive Question Answering
paper.abstract: Long-horizon interactive agents often accumulate large trajectory histories yet still fail to answer questions about earlier events reliably. We argue that the main bottleneck is not context length alone, but the trajectory-to-answer interface of long-term memory. When histories are stored as plain-text chunks and queried with standard retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), systems often retrieve locally relevant but chain-incomplete evidence, especially for spatial, temporal, repeated-event, and

summary.core_problem: 解决长时程交互式智能体在回答早期事件相关问题时，单靠长上下文或普通RAG仍经常检索到局部相关但证据链不完整内容的问题。
summary.importance: 这是一个 agent 长时记忆接口设计问题，不是基座预训练问题本身；价值主要在于说明“记忆表示与检索接口”比单纯拉长上下文更关键，对做长期交互 agent 或 memory-augmented LM 的人有参考意义。
summary.technical_approach: 提出 S3Mem，将轨迹写入结构化的 scene-event episodic memory，而不是纯文本块；检索时使用 anchor-sensitive retrieval，尽量围绕时空锚点、重复事件和多跳状态组织证据；回答阶段再暴露一个紧凑、受 token budget 约束的 evidence interface，减少模型在长轨迹中自行拼接证据链的负担。
summary.experiments: 摘要只说明在两个内部长时程交互 QA 基准上评测，重点覆盖空间、时间、重复事件和多跳状态问题；未在摘要中给出模型规模、训练数据量、具体 baseline 和量化提升幅度，因此目前更像一个系统接口思路，需看正文确认实验是否干净、是否优于更强长上下文和更强检索基线。

summary_en.core_problem: It targets the failure of long-horizon interactive agents to answer questions about earlier events, where longer context or vanilla RAG still retrieves locally relevant but chain-incomplete evidence.
summary_en.importance: This is mainly an agent memory-interface paper rather than a foundation pretraining paper; its value is in showing that memory representation and retrieval interfaces can matter more than raw context length for long-horizon agents.
summary_en.technical_approach: S3Mem writes trajectories into structured scene-event episodic memory instead of plain text chunks. At query time, it uses anchor-sensitive retrieval to organize evidence around spatial/temporal anchors, repeated events, and multi-hop state dependencies, then exposes a compact token-budget-aware evidence interface for answer generation.
summary_en.experiments: The abstract mentions evaluation on two internal long-horizon interactive QA benchmarks, focusing on spatial, temporal, repeated-event, and multi-hop state questions. It does not provide model sizes, training data, baselines, or exact gains, so the current signal is more about system design than a fully validated methodological result.

recommendation.zh: 不是 pretrain 论文，但如果你在做 memory-augmented agent，只看“结构化轨迹写入+检索接口”这件事即可；先别把它当长上下文替代结论。
recommendation.en: Not a pretraining paper, but if you work on memory-augmented agents, read it for the structured write/retrieval interface only; do not treat it as a clean long-context replacement result yet.

paper.title: WorldMemArena: Evaluating Multimodal Agent Memory Through Action-World Interaction
paper.abstract: Multimodal large language models are increasingly deployed as long-horizon agents, where memory must do more than recall: it must track an evolving world, revise what has gone stale, and surface the right evidence at decision time. Existing benchmarks measure recall over static dialogue, collapse memory into a single end-of-task accuracy, and reduce visual observations to captions, leaving us unable to localize failures to writing, maintenance, retrieval, or use. The rise of agent harnesses that

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作要解决的不是“模型能记住多少内容”，而是多模态长程 agent 在动态世界里，记忆系统到底在哪个环节失效。作者指出，现有 memory benchmark 大多把问题压缩成静态上下文里的 recall 或最终问答准确率，因此无法区分：信息有没有被写入、世界变化后有没有更新、需要时有没有被正确取回、取回后有没有真正用于决策。对带执行轨迹的 agent 来说，这个问题更尖锐，因为记忆不再只是外挂数据库，而是和策略、工具调用、环境反馈一起形成闭环。论文因此把 memory 重新定义为一个 Action–World Interaction Loop 中的四阶段生命周期：writing、maintenance、retrieval、use，并围绕这个过程做可诊断评测。
summary.importance: 它的价值主要在评测范式，而不是提出新的 memory 算法。对基座研究的意义有两层。第一，它把“长上下文/外部记忆是否有效”从单点终局指标拆成过程指标，这对分析 agent memory、长上下文建模、RAG-style memory、self-authored memory 都有帮助。第二，它把多模态证据和环境状态变化纳入 memory 评测，避免把视觉观察先压成 caption 再评估，这更接近未来原生多模态 agent 的训练与诊断需求。对做 pretrain/post-train 接口的人，这篇文章提供了一个很实用的视角：很多失败并不是存不进去，而是存了也不会用，或者世界变了但记忆没被修正。这个区分会直接影响训练信号设计。
summary.technical_approach:
方法上，作者先给出一个较清晰的形式化。环境有潜在状态 z_t，agent 只能看到由 Ω 映射得到的局部 observation o_t；策略 π 基于 observation 和当前 memory state m_t 选择 action a_t；环境 ℰ 执行动作后更新状态并返回 feedback f_t。完整轨迹写成 τ=(x;η_1,...,η_T)，其中 η_t=(o_t,a_t,f_t)，再进一步切成多 session 轨迹，使得局部上下文受限，但世界状态跨 session 持续演化。这个设定很关键，因为它把“记忆”从长 prompt 内的被动保留，变成跨 session 的主动状态管理。

在这个框架下，作者定义四个可观测阶段。writing 关注系统是否把未来有用的信息写入 memory；maintenance 关注世界状态变化后，旧记忆是否被修订、删除或标记失效；retrieval 关注回答或决策时是否取回了正确证据；use 关注取回的证据是否真的支撑了最终行为，而不是只是表面命中。论文的一个设计重点，是为这四个阶段提供共享的 trajectory-level gold evidence，而不是让每个指标各自依赖不同标注口径。

基于这个定义，作者构建了 WorldMemArena。数据由 400 个长程多模态交互任务组成，覆盖两类场景。Lifelong Evolution 更像跨 session 的持续状态跟踪，强调个人信息、任务状态、偏好或环境条件的长期变化与复用；Agentic Execution 更接近真实 agent 执行，关键信息分散在 observation、action、tool feedback 和环境变化中，要求系统从执行过程里抽取可复用证据，而不是依赖整理好的叙事文本。每个 session 都标注了 gold memory points、state updates、distractors 和 answer-supporting evidence chains，因此可以分别诊断写入、维护、检索、使用四个环节。

论文还统一比较了三类 memory 范式：长上下文直接塞进 prompt 的 agent、人工设计的 memory pipeline、以及依托 agent harness 让模型自己编写和重组 memory 的系统。这个比较的重点不是谁最终分数高，而是不同范式在四阶段上的失效模式：人工系统通常结构更规整，写入和检索更可控，但适应性差；harness-based memory 更灵活，能在执行中自组织记忆，但成本更高，稳定性也更差。
summary.experiments:
从全文可见的关键信息看，评测集规模是 400 个多 session 长程任务，覆盖 Lifelong Evolution 和 Agentic Execution 两个 regime。作者在统一设置下比较了三类代表性 memory 系统，并给出四个主要经验结论。

第一，写入更多正确记忆点，并不自动带来更好的最终表现。也就是说，memory quantity 和 downstream utility 之间并不是线性关系。很多系统在 writing 指标上不差，但在 use 阶段掉得很明显，说明问题不在“有没有记住”，而在“决策时能否把证据接上”。

第二，多模态 memory 仍是明显瓶颈，尤其在需要复杂视觉推理时更突出。论文强调，若把视觉证据简化成 caption，会掩盖真实困难；在原始多模态交互里，系统更容易在写入和检索阶段丢失视觉细节，最终影响 use。

第三，不同 domain 的 memory 表现差异很大，而且在 Agentic Execution 上普遍比 Lifelong Evolution 更差。原因是后者的信息来源更分散，既包含观察，也包含动作结果、工具反馈和状态变化，memory system 需要从“过程”中抽取证据，而不是从静态文本中摘录事实。

第四，人工 memory 系统与 harness-based memory agent 呈现明显取舍：前者更结构化，但对开放环境变化不够灵活；后者更能适应复杂执行轨迹，但代价更高，且可靠性不足。摘要和正文节选里没有给出完整的数值表，因此这里不编造具体分数；精读时应重点看各阶段指标、不同任务类型分层结果，以及 error case 对四阶段失效的归因。
summary.reading_guide:
这篇适合按“问题定义—数据构造—诊断结论”三步读。

先看 Introduction 和 Problem Formulation。重点不是形式化本身，而是作者为什么坚持把 memory 拆成四阶段，以及为什么要用 session 化的动态世界，而不是长对话。这里决定了整篇工作的评测哲学。

然后看 benchmark 构造部分，尤其是 Lifelong Evolution 与 Agentic Execution 的差别、gold memory points / state updates / evidence chains 的标注方式。这里值得细看，因为很多 benchmark 的上限其实由标注口径决定；如果标注只覆盖显式文本事实，就很难真正测到 agent memory。

实验部分建议优先看三类 memory 范式的对比表，以及四阶段指标和最终任务成功率之间的关系。如果有图表展示 writing 与 use 的脱钩、不同模态或不同任务类型上的退化，这些是最有信息量的地方。

如果时间有限，预计 25 到 35 分钟可以抓住主线；如果要把它当作 agent memory 研究的评测底座来用，建议再花时间看附录中的标注协议、任务示例和 failure case。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper is not asking whether an agent can retain more tokens. It asks where multimodal memory actually breaks in long-horizon interaction with a changing world. Existing memory benchmarks mostly test recall in static dialogue or collapse everything into final QA accuracy. That setup cannot tell whether useful evidence was written at all, whether stale memory was updated after the world changed, whether the right evidence was retrieved at decision time, or whether retrieved evidence was truly used. This becomes more important for execution-based agents, where memory is intertwined with policy, tool feedback, and environment transitions. The paper therefore reframes agent memory as a four-stage lifecycle inside an Action–World Interaction Loop: writing, maintenance, retrieval, and use.
summary_en.importance: Its main contribution is an evaluation lens rather than a new memory algorithm. For foundation-model research, the value is twofold. First, it decomposes memory quality into process-level signals instead of a single end metric. That is useful for studying long-context agents, external memory systems, retrieval-augmented memory, and self-authored memory. Second, it keeps multimodal evidence and world-state evolution in the loop, instead of reducing visual observations to captions before evaluation. That makes the benchmark more relevant to native multimodal agents. For people working on the pretrain/post-train interface, the paper offers a practical diagnosis: many failures are not about failing to store information, but about failing to revise or use it when the environment changes.
summary_en.technical_approach:
The paper starts with a clean formalization. The environment has a latent state z_t. The agent only observes partial inputs o_t through an observation mapping Ω. A policy π chooses action a_t based on the current observation and memory state m_t. The environment ℰ executes the action, updates the world, and returns feedback f_t. A full trajectory is written as τ=(x;η_1,...,η_T), where each event η_t=(o_t,a_t,f_t). The trajectory is further segmented into multiple sessions, so local context is limited while the world state persists across sessions. This is an important design choice: memory is treated as active state management across sessions, not passive retention inside one long prompt.

On top of this setup, the paper defines four observable stages. Writing asks whether future-useful information is stored. Maintenance asks whether memory is revised, deleted, or marked stale when the world changes. Retrieval asks whether the correct evidence is surfaced when answering or acting. Use asks whether the retrieved evidence actually supports the final decision rather than being superficially present. A notable design choice is that all four stages are grounded in shared trajectory-level gold evidence, which makes diagnosis more consistent.

The benchmark, WorldMemArena, contains 400 long-horizon multimodal interaction tasks spanning two regimes. Lifelong Evolution focuses on persistent personal or task states that evolve across sessions and must be tracked and reused over time. Agentic Execution is closer to realistic agent trajectories, where reusable evidence is distributed across observations, actions, tool feedback, and state changes rather than packaged as clean text narratives. Each session is annotated with gold memory points, state updates, distractors, and answer-supporting evidence chains, enabling stage-level diagnosis.

The paper then evaluates three representative memory paradigms under one setup: long-context agents that rely on prompt accumulation, manually designed memory pipelines, and harness-based memory agents that author and reorganize their own memory during execution. The comparison is useful because it exposes different failure modes rather than only ranking systems by final accuracy. Manual systems tend to be more structured and controllable, while harness-based systems are more adaptive but also more expensive and less reliable.
summary_en.experiments:
From the full text provided, the benchmark contains 400 multi-session long-horizon tasks across Lifelong Evolution and Agentic Execution. The paper compares three classes of memory systems and reports four main empirical findings.

First, storing more correct memory items does not guarantee better downstream performance. Memory quantity and memory utility are clearly decoupled. Some systems do reasonably well on writing but still fail badly at use, which means the bottleneck is often decision-time integration rather than storage.

Second, multimodal memory remains a major bottleneck, especially on tasks requiring nontrivial visual reasoning. The paper explicitly argues that caption-based evaluation hides this difficulty. In native multimodal interaction, visual details are more easily lost during writing and retrieval, which then hurts use.

Third, performance varies substantially by domain and degrades on Agentic Execution relative to Lifelong Evolution. The reason is that evidence in Agentic Execution is distributed across the interaction process itself, including actions and tool feedback, not just observations. Memory systems therefore need to extract reusable evidence from trajectories rather than copy facts from text.

Fourth, manual memory systems and harness-based memory agents show a clear trade-off. Manual systems are more structured but less adaptive. Harness-based systems are more flexible in open-ended execution but remain costly and less reliable. The excerpt does not include the full numeric tables, so it is better not to invent exact scores. The most informative parts to inspect are the stage-level metrics, the gap between writing and use, and the breakdown by task regime and modality.
summary_en.reading_guide:
Read it in three passes: problem framing, benchmark construction, and diagnosis.

Start with the Introduction and Problem Formulation. The key point is not the notation itself, but why the authors insist on a four-stage lifecycle and a session-based dynamic world instead of long dialogue. That choice defines the benchmark’s philosophy.

Then read the benchmark construction carefully, especially the difference between Lifelong Evolution and Agentic Execution, and how gold memory points, state updates, and evidence chains are annotated. This is worth attention because the usefulness of a memory benchmark depends heavily on what is labeled as evidence.

In the experiments, prioritize the comparison across the three memory paradigms and the relationship between stage-level metrics and final task success. Any figure showing the disconnect between writing and use, or degradation by modality and task type, is likely to be the most informative.

If you only need the main idea, 25–35 minutes should be enough. If you want to reuse it as an evaluation scaffold for agent memory work, spend extra time on the annotation protocol, task examples, and failure cases in the appendix.

recommendation.zh: 将agent记忆拆解为四阶段生命周期并建立可诊断的评测框架，这种设计方法论对思考通用agent能力评估范式有借鉴价值，建议看评测设计章节。
recommendation.en: The four-stage lifecycle decomposition of agent memory and diagnosable evaluation design methodology is insightful for thinking about general agent capability assessment paradigms. Read the evaluation design section.

paper.title: STAMP: Training Explicit Memory for Mobile GUI Agents in Controllable and Scalable Virtual Environments
paper.abstract: Mobile GUI agents excel at immediate reactive control but frequently fail in realistic, long-horizon tasks that require memory. This failure stems from a fundamental conflict between limited context windows and token-heavy screenshots. To save the limited context, agents must progressively discard older visual history, permanently losing crucial transient information. Furthermore, existing action-centric datasets fail to teach agents what or when to explicitly memorize, and augmenting static rea

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作解决移动 GUI agent 在长时程任务中因上下文窗口有限、截图 token 过重而遗忘关键历史信息的问题。
summary.importance: 贡献属于 agent 训练范式与数据生成：不是基座预训练，但对“显式记忆是否应被监督训练出来”这个问题给了较干净的环境化方案。对做长上下文、外部记忆、agent training 的研究员有边际启发。
summary.technical_approach: STAMP 在可控虚拟环境中程序化注入 deterministic memory variables，精确控制什么信息必须记、何时编码、何时检索，从而自动生成可验证监督数据；同时支持在线强化学习训练，让 agent 学会显式 memory write/read，而不是完全依赖上下文堆叠。
summary.experiments: 摘要表明实验聚焦 mobile GUI 长时程任务，对比现有 reactive agents 和 action-centric 数据训练方案，验证显式记忆训练在长任务上的收益。未给出具体 benchmark、模型规模和提升幅度，因此当前更像一个训练框架提案，需看正文确认 setup 是否干净、是否超越简单 retrieval baselines。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper addresses the failure of mobile GUI agents on long-horizon tasks, where limited context windows and token-heavy screenshots cause the agent to forget crucial transient information.
summary_en.importance: This is an agent-training and data-generation contribution rather than foundation-model pretraining. Its main value is a relatively clean setup for studying whether explicit memory should be trained under supervision, which may still be useful for researchers working on long-context, external memory, or agent training.
summary_en.technical_approach: STAMP builds controllable virtual environments with programmatically injected deterministic memory variables, so the training pipeline can specify what must be memorized, when it should be encoded, and when it must be retrieved. This yields verifiable supervised data at scale and also supports online RL for explicit memory write/read behavior.
summary_en.experiments: The abstract suggests evaluations on long-horizon mobile GUI tasks against reactive agents and action-centric training data. It claims gains from explicit memory training, but provides no concrete benchmarks, model sizes, or margins, so the real value depends on whether the full paper cleanly rules out simpler retrieval or context-management baselines.

recommendation.zh: 不是 pretrain 论文，但“可控环境里把记忆变量显式监督出来”这个 setup 还算干净；若你做 agent memory，只看数据生成和 RL 设计。
recommendation.en: Not a pretraining paper, but the controlled supervision of explicit memory variables is a fairly clean setup; if you work on agent memory, read only the data-generation and RL parts.

paper.title: AutoScientists: Self-Organizing Agent Teams for Long-Running Scientific Experimentation
paper.abstract: Scientific research proceeds through iterative cycles of hypothesis generation, experiment design, execution, and revision. AI agents can automate parts of this process, but existing approaches typically follow a single research trajectory or coordinate through a central planner with fixed objectives. As a result, they struggle to sustain parallel exploration, adapt as experimental evidence changes, or preserve knowledge of failed directions over long-running experiments. We introduce AutoScient

summary.core_problem: 解决长周期科学实验自动化中，单轨迹或中心化 agent 难以并行探索、随证据更新方向、并保留失败经验的问题。
summary.importance: 这是一个多 agent 系统工作，和 LLM 基座预训练的直接关系不强。它的保留价值主要在于：把长期实验搜索看成去中心化协作与在线资源分配问题，而不是固定 planner 的流水线。这对自动化研究、实验调度和 agent memory 设计有一定参考，但不直接推进 pretrain 方法论。
summary.technical_approach: 作者提出 AutoScientists，一个 decentralized team of AI agents。系统让多个 agent 读取共享实验状态，自组织成围绕不同假设的团队，在消耗实验算力前先互相 critique，并共享成功与失败经验以减少重复探索。方法重点是去中心化组织、并行假设探索、失败知识保留，而不是新的基础模型训练目标。
summary.experiments: 实验覆盖 biomedical machine learning、language-model training optimization、protein fitness prediction 等长周期计算实验任务，并在匹配实验预算下优于先前 AI agent。摘要没有给出底层模型、任务规模、提升幅度和对比系统细节，因此目前只能把它视为 agent orchestration 的系统性尝试。
summary.authors_note: Marinka Zitnik 是计算生物与图机器学习方向较知名的研究者。

summary_en.core_problem: It tackles the difficulty of automating long-running scientific experimentation, where single-trajectory or centralized agents struggle with parallel exploration, evidence-driven adaptation, and remembering failed directions.
summary_en.importance: This is a multi-agent systems paper with limited direct relevance to foundation-model pretraining. Its main value is conceptual: it frames long-horizon experimentation as decentralized coordination and online resource allocation rather than a fixed planner pipeline. That is useful for automated research systems, but it does not directly advance pretraining methodology.
summary_en.technical_approach: The paper introduces AutoScientists, a decentralized team of AI agents. Agents read a shared experimental state, self-organize into teams around promising hypotheses, critique proposals before spending experimental compute, and share both successes and failures to reduce redundant exploration. The contribution is in decentralized organization, parallel hypothesis search, and memory of failed attempts, not in a new base-model training objective.
summary_en.experiments: The evaluation spans biomedical machine learning, language-model training optimization, and protein fitness prediction, with gains over prior AI agents under matched experimental budgets. The abstract does not provide the underlying model stack, task scales, exact margins, or detailed baselines, so it is best treated as a systems-level agent paper for now.
summary_en.authors_note: Marinka Zitnik is a well-known researcher in computational biology and graph machine learning.

recommendation.zh: 和 pretrain 关系偏远，只需知道它把长期实验搜索做成去中心化多 agent；若你在做自动化 research loop，可看系统设计，否则不必读正文。
recommendation.en: Only worth knowing if you build automated research loops: it turns long-horizon experimentation into decentralized multi-agent search; otherwise it is far from core pretraining.

paper.title: MemFail: Stress-Testing Failure Modes of LLM Memory Systems
paper.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly rely on external memory systems to remain consistent across long-horizon interactions, but little empirical work has been done to understand the specific failure modes and design choices that these systems present. Existing benchmarks report aggregate question-answering accuracy and treat memory systems as black boxes, making it impossible to attribute an incorrect answer to a particular failure mode of the system. We introduce MemFail, a diagnostic

summary.core_problem: 现有 LLM 记忆系统评测通常将其视为黑盒，只报告端到端的问答准确率，无法定位具体是哪个环节（总结、存储、检索或推理）导致了失败。
summary.importance: 提出了一个诊断性评测基准 MemFail，将记忆系统解耦为总结、存储和检索三个规范操作，并针对性地设计了五组任务来隔离和测试这些操作的失败模式，为记忆系统的架构设计和优化提供了更细粒度的诊断工具。
summary.technical_approach: 将记忆系统形式化为总结（压缩对话历史）、存储（更新记忆库）和检索（提取相关记忆）三个步骤。基于此，构建了五个数据集：Conditional-Facts（测试因果关系保留）、Persona-Retrieval（测试误导性问题下的细节保留）、Long-Hop（测试长程因果检索）、Coexisting-Facts（测试共存事实的存储和检索）和 Conditional-Facts (Hard)（测试总结时的细节保留）。
summary.experiments: 在 MemFail 上评估了 Mem0、A-MEM、SimpleMem 和 StructMem。结果表明，没有单一系统在所有任务上占优，每种架构都有独特的失败模式（例如基于图的 StructMem 擅长因果推理但在共存事实检索上表现不佳）。此外，增加检索记忆数量或使用更强的底层 LLM 带来的提升有限，甚至可能导致性能下降，说明当前系统的瓶颈在于架构设计而非模型能力或上下文窗口。
summary.reading_guide: 建议重点阅读 Introduction 中对记忆系统操作的解耦（总结、存储、检索）以及 Background 中对失败模式的定义。实验部分关注不同系统在特定任务上的表现差异，这对于理解不同记忆架构的优劣非常有帮助。

summary_en.core_problem: Existing evaluations of LLM memory systems treat them as black boxes, reporting only end-to-end QA accuracy without isolating which specific component (summarization, storage, retrieval, or reasoning) caused the failure.
summary_en.importance: Introduces MemFail, a diagnostic benchmark that decouples memory systems into three canonical operations (summarization, storage, and retrieval) and designs five specific tasks to isolate and test the failure modes of these operations, providing a fine-grained diagnostic tool for memory system architecture design and optimization.
summary_en.technical_approach: Formalizes memory systems into three steps: summarization (compressing conversation history), storage (updating the memory database), and retrieval (extracting relevant memories). Based on this, constructs five datasets: Conditional-Facts (testing retention of causal relationships), Persona-Retrieval (testing detail retention under misleading questions), Long-Hop (testing long-range causal retrieval), Coexisting-Facts (testing storage and retrieval of coexisting facts), and Conditional-Facts (Hard) (testing detail retention during summarization).
summary_en.experiments: Evaluated Mem0, A-MEM, SimpleMem, and StructMem on MemFail. Results show no single system dominates; each architecture has a distinct failure signature (e.g., graph-based StructMem excels at causal reasoning but fails on coexisting-fact retrieval). Furthermore, scaling the number of retrieved memories or the underlying LLM strength yields limited improvement and sometimes degrades performance, indicating current bottlenecks are architectural rather than model capability or context window size.
summary_en.reading_guide: Focus on the decoupling of memory system operations (summarization, storage, retrieval) in the Introduction and the definition of failure modes in the Background. In the experiments section, pay attention to the performance differences of various systems on specific tasks, which is crucial for understanding the pros and cons of different memory architectures.

recommendation.zh: 读 benchmark taxonomy 和错误归因表；memory 不是 pretrain 核心，但这类失败分解会影响长程 agent 数据设计。
recommendation.en: Read the benchmark taxonomy and attribution tables; memory is not core pretraining, but this failure decomposition matters for long-horizon agent data design.

paper.title: SEC-bench Pro: Can Language Models Solve Long-Horizon Software Security Tasks?
paper.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) now support automated software security tasks, including vulnerability discovery and proof-of-concept (PoC) generation. Existing benchmarks do not faithfully evaluate LLMs in real-world bug hunting scenarios because they rely on fuzzing harnesses, target-specific descriptions, or vulnerability-reproduction tasks. We present SEC-bench Pro, a benchmark for measuring agent bug hunting on critical, high-complexity software systems. This work discloses reports with concre

summary.core_problem: 论文提出 SEC-bench Pro，用来评测 LLM agent 在真实大型软件中的长程漏洞挖掘能力，尤其是从公开代码和历史版本中发现并构造 PoC，而不是在给定 harness、漏洞描述或 sanitizer 线索的条件下复现已知问题。
summary.importance: 这是评测类工作，对基座预训练的直接方法贡献有限，但对 code agent 和长程软件工程能力评估有参考价值。它把安全任务评测从短路径、强提示、harness 驱动的复现，推向更接近实际审计的设置。对预训练研究的启发在于：当前代码模型的能力瓶颈不只在语法生成或局部修补，而在长上下文代码理解、动态执行证据整合、假设管理、失败恢复和安全领域知识的组合。
summary.technical_approach: SEC-bench Pro 的核心是一个可持续扩展的 benchmark 构建流水线。第一阶段从 issue tracker 和 advisory feed 收集安全报告、PoC 输入和关联修复。第二阶段用 coding agent 重建历史 vulnerable 环境，并重新验证收集到的 PoC。第三阶段通过 construction oracles 验证 vulnerable、fixed、latest 三个镜像，确保任务可复现。每个实例以 Docker image triples 发布。评测时，agent 需要提交 PoC；grading harness 会在三个镜像上执行，并用 LLM judge 判断证据是否指向目标漏洞，而不是无关 crash。这个设计减少了目标函数泄漏，也避免只靠 exit code 或 patch pattern 造成误判。
summary.experiments: 数据集包含 183 个验证过的 JavaScript 引擎漏洞实例，其中 V8 103 个，SpiderMonkey 80 个。V8 子集包含 Google VRP 奖励累计超过 150 万美元的 bounty-qualified 报告。漏洞类型覆盖 use-after-free、type confusion、out-of-bounds access、sandbox bypass、JIT 相关问题等。论文评测了三个 coding-agent scaffold：Codex 使用 OpenAI GPT-5.4，ClaudeCode 使用 Anthropic Opus 4.6，OpenCode 使用 Moonshot Kimi-K2.6。所有配置在两个引擎上成功率都低于 40%。最强单配置解决 V8 33/103、SpiderMonkey 31/80；Kimi-K2.6 open-weight baseline 在 V8 上为 12/103。ClaudeCode 与 Codex 有互补性，二者并集覆盖 V8 39/103、SpiderMonkey 39/80。失败样本通常消耗更多 token，许多被拒 PoC 要么在 vulnerable image 上正常退出，要么触发了与目标漏洞无关的 crash。
summary.reading_guide: 建议泛读，预计 25–35 分钟。优先看 benchmark construction pipeline、oracle validation、grading protocol，以及 baseline failure analysis。若关注 agent 训练数据和评测闭环，可以重点看失败 PoC 的分类、token 消耗与成功率关系、Codex 和 ClaudeCode 的互补解集。JS 引擎背景部分可按需阅读，主要用于理解为什么 V8 和 SpiderMonkey 能测试长程安全推理。

summary_en.core_problem: SEC-bench Pro evaluates whether LLM agents can perform long-horizon bug hunting on large production software systems. The target setting is closer to real security auditing: agents must discover and demonstrate vulnerabilities without being handed a fuzzing harness, target-specific hints, or sanitizer-style vulnerability descriptions.
summary_en.importance: This is primarily an evaluation contribution. It is not a pretraining method paper, but it is useful for understanding the capability gaps of code models and software agents. The benchmark stresses long-context repository understanding, execution-guided reasoning, hypothesis refinement, failure recovery, and domain knowledge in browser engine security. These are capability dimensions that are easy to miss in short coding benchmarks.
summary_en.technical_approach: The benchmark is built through a three-phase pipeline. First, it collects disclosed security reports, PoC inputs, and linked fixes from issue trackers and advisory feeds. Second, coding agents reconstruct the historical vulnerable environments and revalidate the collected PoCs. Third, construction oracles validate vulnerable, fixed, and latest Docker images before an instance is admitted. Each task ships as a Docker image triple. During evaluation, submitted PoCs are executed across the three images, and an LLM judge checks whether the evidence demonstrates the intended vulnerability rather than an unrelated crash. This design reduces information leakage and avoids brittle grading based only on exit codes, patch patterns, or crash signatures.
summary_en.experiments: SEC-bench Pro contains 183 validated vulnerabilities from JavaScript engines: 103 from V8 and 80 from SpiderMonkey. The V8 subset includes bounty-qualified reports with cumulative Google VRP awards above $1.5 million. The dataset covers use-after-free, type confusion, out-of-bounds access, sandbox bypass, JIT-related failures, and other memory-safety classes. The paper evaluates Codex with OpenAI GPT-5.4, ClaudeCode with Anthropic Opus 4.6, and OpenCode with Moonshot Kimi-K2.6. All configurations remain below 40% success on both engines. The strongest single setup solves 33/103 V8 tasks and 31/80 SpiderMonkey tasks. The open-weight Kimi-K2.6 baseline solves 12/103 V8 tasks. Codex and ClaudeCode solve partially complementary sets, with their union covering 39/103 V8 and 39/80 SpiderMonkey instances. Failed runs tend to consume more tokens, and many rejected PoCs either exit cleanly on the vulnerable image or crash outside the target attribution boundary.
summary_en.reading_guide: Skim in 25–35 minutes. Focus on the construction pipeline, oracle validation, grading protocol, and failure analysis. For researchers interested in agent training and evaluation loops, the most useful parts are the rejected-PoC taxonomy, token-use analysis, and complementarity between Codex and ClaudeCode. The JavaScript engine background is useful if one needs context on why V8 and SpiderMonkey create hard long-horizon security tasks.

recommendation.zh: 读任务构造和 oracle 验证即可；它是检验 coding agent 长程安全能力的硬样本池，不直接教你训练。
recommendation.en: Read the task construction and oracle validation; it is a hard testbed for long-horizon security agents, not a training recipe.

paper.title: Claw-Anything: Benchmarking Always-On Personal Assistants with Broader Access to User's Digital World
paper.abstract: Large language model agents are increasingly envisioned as always-on personal assistants with access to anything relevant in the user's digital world. Yet current systems operate over only narrow slices of that world, limiting context-sensitive reasoning and effective assistance. Existing benchmarks similarly provide only partial user state and therefore fail to capture performance in such a broad, always-on setting. To address this gap, we introduce Claw-Anything, a benchmark that expands agent

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作解决的是 always-on personal assistant 的评测失真问题。现有 benchmark 往往只给 agent 一个狭窄、静态、局部的用户状态切片，因此模型看起来能做任务，但并没有真正面对“长期历史、多服务依赖、多设备交互”这些现实约束。Claw-Anything 想回答的是：如果把 agent 放进更接近真实数字生活的环境里，要求它利用长期事件流、跨后端服务状态、GUI/CLI 混合接口去完成 reactive 和 proactive 任务，现有模型到底还剩多少能力。
summary.importance: 对预训练研究的直接关系不强，但对 agent 训练数据和后训练评测有现实意义。它的重要性主要在两层。第一，它把 agent 的“可访问数字世界范围”明确提出为核心变量，而不是只看模型推理本身。这会影响后续很多训练设计：如果训练环境没有长期状态和跨系统依赖，模型学到的只是短程 scripted behavior。第二，它不只是 benchmark，还提供了可扩展的数据生成管线，并展示用这些环境生成成功轨迹去微调模型能带来明显提升。对做 agent mid-train、trajectory SFT、environment simulation 的人，这篇有方法资产价值；对纯 LLM pretrain 则更多是边界相关工作。
summary.technical_approach:
方法核心是构建一个更宽上下文范围的 agent benchmark。作者把扩展分成三维：长时程活动历史、相互依赖的后端服务、以及多设备上的 GUI/CLI 交互。与很多现有环境只暴露单应用或单轮任务不同，这里 agent 需要在一个持续演化的 persona-grounded digital world 中行动。

环境构建采用自动化合成管线。起点是一个最小 persona seed，然后用 LLM-based simulator 做 multi-round event injection，逐轮向用户世界中注入日常事件，并同步更新 persistent world state 和各类动态服务痕迹，比如邮件、日历、社交平台等。随着轮次增加，历史会累积，persona 会被逐步具体化，环境中也会出现噪声、无关事件甚至相互矛盾的信息。最后把“下一事件”实例化成一个 grounded task，并配一个 executable verifier，于是评测变成：agent 是否能在这个不断演化的数字生活里完成下一步合适动作。

这个设计有两个值得注意的点。其一，任务不是脱离环境单独写出来的，而是从环境演化过程中自然长出来，因此更容易包含跨时间依赖和隐含前提。其二，作者把 proactive assistance 也纳入评测，要求模型不是只响应显式指令，而是从上下文中推断用户可能需要什么。这比传统 benchmark 更接近 always-on assistant 的真实目标。
summary.experiments:
主实验结论很直接：在 Claw-Anything 上，GPT-5.5 的 pass@1 只有 34.5%，明显低于很多模型在既有 benchmark 上的表现。作者据此认为，现有 benchmark 低估了长期状态整合、跨服务协调和多设备操作带来的难度。这个结论对评测设计是成立的，因为 benchmark 的核心价值就在于暴露旧基准覆盖不到的失败模式。

数据规模方面，论文构建了 200 个 human-verified evaluation tasks，以及 2,000 个 training environments。更关键的是，它验证了这些训练环境不只是“能生成数据”，而是能转化成有效监督：用从其中得到的 1,500 条 successful trajectories 去微调 Qwen3.5-27B，成功率提升 23.7%。这个数字说明环境模拟和任务合成至少在 agent 后训练上是有用的。

从研究者视角，最值得关注的不是谁在榜单上第一，而是性能掉得有多厉害，以及微调后能回升多少。前者说明现有 agent 能力对环境复杂度很敏感；后者说明数据缺口可能比架构缺口更大，至少在这一类任务上如此。
summary.reading_guide:
这篇按 skim 读即可。先看 Introduction 和 Figure 1/2，理解作者定义的三种 context expansion 到底是什么，以及为什么现有 benchmark 不够。然后看环境合成管线，重点关注 multi-round event injection、persistent state 更新、task/verifier 生成这三步。最后看实验部分，确认 benchmark 难度来自哪里：是长历史、跨服务依赖，还是多设备交互。

如果只有 15–20 分钟，建议读法是：引言 → benchmark 构造方法 → 主结果表 → 微调实验。若要多花一点时间，优先看 human verification 和 executable verifier 的设计，因为 benchmark 是否可信，主要取决于任务是否真的可执行、可判定，而不是环境描述写得多复杂。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper addresses an evaluation mismatch for always-on personal assistants. Most existing benchmarks expose only narrow, static slices of user state, so agents are tested in settings that miss the core difficulties of real assistance: long activity histories, cross-service dependencies, and interaction across multiple devices and interfaces. Claw-Anything asks a simple but important question: once agents are placed in a broader digital world, how much capability remains?
summary_en.importance: Its relevance to core LM pretraining is limited, but it matters for agent training data, post-training, and evaluation design. Two contributions stand out. First, it makes the scope of accessible user state an explicit variable in agent evaluation, rather than treating the environment as a fixed backdrop. That matters because training on narrow environments can produce brittle, scripted behavior that does not transfer to realistic assistance. Second, the work is not only a benchmark; it also provides a scalable environment-and-task generation pipeline and shows that trajectories derived from it can improve an open model through fine-tuning. For researchers working on agent mid-training, trajectory SFT, or synthetic environment generation, that is the main reason to read it.
summary_en.technical_approach:
The core idea is to benchmark agents under a much broader operational scope. The environment is expanded along three axes: long-horizon event histories, interdependent backend services, and multi-device interaction through both GUI and CLI. Unlike many prior benchmarks that isolate a single app or a single-turn task, Claw-Anything embeds each task inside an evolving, persona-grounded digital world.

The environment is built through an automated synthesis pipeline. Starting from a minimal persona seed, an LLM-based simulator performs multi-round event injection, incrementally adding everyday events and updating both persistent world state and dynamic service traces such as email, calendars, and social platforms. As the process continues, the event history grows, the persona becomes more specific, and the environment accumulates realistic noise, including irrelevant and contradictory events. The next event is then turned into a grounded task with an executable verifier, so evaluation becomes a question of whether the agent can perform the appropriate next action in an evolving digital life.

Two design choices are especially notable. First, tasks emerge from the simulated world rather than being written independently of it, which makes temporal dependencies and hidden assumptions more natural. Second, the benchmark includes proactive assistance, so agents are evaluated not only on responding to explicit requests but also on inferring useful actions from context.
summary_en.experiments:
The main empirical result is straightforward: GPT-5.5 reaches only 34.5% pass@1 on Claw-Anything, much lower than the performance many models report on earlier benchmarks. The intended conclusion is that prior evaluations underrepresent the difficulty of integrating long histories, coordinating across services, and acting across devices. For a benchmark paper, that is the key result.

In terms of scale, the paper builds 200 human-verified evaluation tasks and 2,000 training environments. More importantly, it shows that these environments are useful beyond evaluation. Fine-tuning Qwen3.5-27B on 1,500 successful trajectories derived from the training environments improves success by 23.7%. That suggests the synthetic pipeline is not merely generating harder tests; it can also produce supervision that helps close part of the capability gap.

From a research perspective, the most informative numbers are not leaderboard rankings but the size of the drop under broader context and the amount recovered through fine-tuning. The first indicates strong sensitivity to environment complexity. The second suggests that data coverage may be a larger bottleneck than architecture, at least for this class of agent tasks.
summary_en.reading_guide:
This is a skim read. Start with the introduction and the main figures to understand the three dimensions of context expansion and why the authors consider current benchmarks insufficient. Then read the environment-generation pipeline, focusing on multi-round event injection, persistent-state updates, and task/verifier construction. Finish with the experiments, asking which source of difficulty matters most: long histories, cross-service dependencies, or multi-device interaction.

If you only have 15–20 minutes, read in this order: introduction, benchmark construction, main results, then the fine-tuning experiment. If you want to inspect one part more carefully, choose the human-verification protocol and the executable verifier design. The credibility of the benchmark depends much more on whether tasks are actually executable and judgeable than on how rich the environment description sounds.

recommendation.zh: 如果你关心 agent eval，这篇该看 benchmark 设计而不是 leaderboard：长历史+噪声事件+跨设备状态很接近真实部署痛点，可拿来校验模型的长期上下文 prior。
recommendation.en: If you care about agent evaluation, read the benchmark design rather than the leaderboard; the long-history, noisy-event, multi-device setup is close to real deployment failure modes.

institutions: Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences

paper.title: MemGym: a Long-Horizon Memory Environment for LLM Agents
paper.abstract: Memory is a central capability for LLM agents operating across long-horizon tasks. Existing memory benchmarks predominantly evaluate retention of personalized information in multi-turn chat scenarios, overlooking the dynamic memory formation that occurs during extended agent execution. Consequently, the memory systems they produce transfer poorly to realistic agentic environments, such as coding and web navigation. We present MemGym, a benchmark for agentic memory that unifies existing agent gym

summary.core_problem: 现有“记忆”评测要么是长上下文/多轮聊天里的静态信息记忆，要么是像 SWE-Gym/WebArena 这类长程 agent 环境但只给端到端成功率，导致记忆失败与推理/工具使用失败纠缠在一起，且评测成本高。论文要解决的是：为长程 agent 的“记忆形成”（保留/压缩/淘汰）提供可分离、可迭代、成本可控的评测与训练闭环。
summary.importance: 对预训练本身影响间接，但对 post-train 与“pretrain↔posttrain 闭环”更相关：它把记忆模块从 reasoner 中剥离，提供 memory-isolated 指标与可规模化的轨迹数据，并用轻量 reward model 替代昂贵环境 rollout，降低了记忆策略/压缩策略的迭代门槛。对基座研究的启发点在于：1）把长程能力拆成可度量的子能力（压缩事件的安全/有害）比只看最终成功率更可优化；2）用小模型 RM 做内环评估，类似把“昂贵外部世界”蒸馏成可学习的判别器信号。
summary.technical_approach:
MemGym 提供统一的 memory–reasoning 接口：把“记忆模块”作为包装 prompt 的独立组件插在 agent loop 中，使每次压缩/写入/淘汰事件都可观测、可记录，并在固定 reasoner 下做 with-memory vs no-memory 的配对对比，从而把分数解释为“记忆带来的增益”。
组成：
- 五条评测轨道：对既有环境的 wrapper（τ²-bench 对话、SWE-Gym 编码、WebArena-Infinity 电脑使用）+ 两条自建的 memory-grounded 轨道（MemGym-DR 深度检索研究、MemGym-CodeQA）。自建轨道强调“可控长度”和“验证确实需要记忆”，避免信息可从参数记忆/环境中轻易再推导。
- 可控合成数据管线：对 MemGym-CodeQA 与 MemGym-DR 生成可调长度实例，并用 ablation（no-memory、distractor-only、leakage-prone 等）验证评测确实在测目标记忆通道。
- MemRM：用收集到的压缩事件轨迹训练一个轻量标量模型，预测“压缩后行为是否保持不变”的概率，用于替代昂贵的 Docker rollout，既可做快速评测也可做后训练奖励信号。实现上用 Qwen3-1.7B + QLoRA 微调。
summary.experiments:
关键结果（文中明确给出的数字）：
- MemRM 在 SWE-Gym IID split 上对压缩事件好坏的判别 AUROC 达到 0.985，可用一次亚秒级分类调用替代一次环境 rollout 作为内环信号。
- 基准覆盖：7 类记忆策略 + None 对照，在 5 个环境上形成 17 个（track, strategy）评测单元，并提供配对的 baseline-vs-memory delta 以隔离记忆效应。
（当前片段未给出各记忆家族在各轨道上的具体分数表；精读实验章节需要补齐：哪些策略在何种 regime 下有效、memory-isolated 指标如何定义与计算、以及 MemRM 与真实 rollout 的相关性/校准曲线。）
summary.reading_guide:
泛读建议按“接口—指标—闭环”顺序：
1）先看 §3.2/§3.3 的统一接口与 memory-isolated 评分定义：它决定了这个 benchmark 是否真的把记忆从推理里拆出来。
2）再看 §3.4 的两条合成管线与 ablation 验证：重点确认是否避免了“看似测记忆、实际靠参数泄漏/可再推导”的假压力。
3）最后看 §4 的 MemRM 训练与替代 rollout 的证据：AUROC 之外，关注误报/漏报代价、跨环境泛化、以及作为 reward 用于训练时是否引入偏置。
预计阅读时间：30–45 分钟可掌握框架与主要结论；若要用它做训练研究，需要额外通读附录里环境 patch、扰动分类与数据格式。

summary_en.core_problem: Memory evaluation for LLM agents is either (a) long-context/static recall in chat, or (b) long-horizon agent benchmarks where only end-task success is reported, entangling memory failures with reasoning/tool-use errors and making iteration expensive. The paper aims to evaluate and train “memory formation” during agent execution—what to keep, compress, or evict—via a unified, memory-isolated, lower-cost loop.
summary_en.importance: Indirect for pretraining, but highly relevant to the pretrain↔post-train loop: it operationalizes memory as a separable module with paired with-memory vs no-memory comparisons under a fixed reasoner, releases trajectory data, and introduces a lightweight reward model to replace costly environment rollouts. The broader lesson is that decomposing long-horizon capability into optimizable sub-signals (compression events) can be more actionable than optimizing only final success.
summary_en.technical_approach:
MemGym unifies five tracks behind a shared memory–reasoning contract where a memory module wraps the prompt sent to the policy LLM. This makes each compression/write/eviction event observable and scorable, and enables paired runs (same reasoner, with vs without memory) so deltas reflect memory effects.
Components:
- Tracks: wrappers for τ²-bench (tool-use dialogue), SWE-Gym (coding), WebArena-Infinity (computer use), plus two in-house memory-grounded tracks (MemGym-DR deep research, MemGym-CodeQA).
- Controllable synthetic pipelines for DR and CodeQA with length tuning and verifier-style ablations (no-memory, distractor-only, leakage-prone) to ensure the benchmark truly induces memory pressure.
- MemRM: a small scalar reward model trained on collected trajectories to predict P(behavior unchanged | compress), used as a fast proxy for expensive Docker rollouts. Implemented as Qwen3-1.7B fine-tuned with QLoRA.
summary_en.experiments:
Explicit reported numbers and coverage:
- MemRM achieves AUROC 0.985 on the SWE-Gym IID split for classifying compression-event outcomes, enabling sub-second scoring instead of full rollouts.
- Evaluation spans 7 memory families plus a None control across 17 (track, strategy) cells over 5 environments, with paired baseline-vs-memory deltas.
(The excerpt does not include the full per-track score tables or detailed definitions of the memory-isolated metrics; those are essential to validate what is being measured and should be extracted from the main experiments/appendices.)
summary_en.reading_guide:
Skim in this order:
1) The interface and memory-isolated scoring definition (§3.2–§3.3): this determines whether the benchmark truly disentangles memory from reasoning.
2) The synthetic pipeline and ablation verification (§3.4): check how they prevent “illusory memory pressure” and leakage.
3) MemRM evidence (§4): beyond AUROC, look for calibration, failure modes, cross-track generalization, and bias when used as a training reward.
Time: ~30–45 minutes for the core framework; longer if you plan to use the benchmark (appendices contain engineering details and data formats).

recommendation.zh: 做 agent memory 的人该看，但对 pretrain 研究员只需抓住它的隔离评测设计；先看任务分解和 memory-isolated score，别被总分带偏。
recommendation.en: Worth reading if you care about agent memory; for pretraining people, the key is the isolation protocol—read the task decomposition and memory-isolated scoring, not the headline leaderboard.

paper.title: π-Bench: Evaluating Proactive Personal Assistant Agents in Long-Horizon Workflows
paper.abstract: The rise of personal assistant agents, e.g., OpenClaw, highlights the growing potential of large language models to support users across everyday life and work. A core challenge in these settings is proactive assistance, since users often begin with underspecified requests and leave important needs, constraints, or preferences unstated. However, existing benchmarks rarely evaluate whether agents can identify and act on such hidden intents before they are explicitly stated, especially in sustaine

summary.core_problem: π-Bench 评估的是长周期个人助理中的主动性问题：用户只给出不完整请求，真实需求藏在偏好、约束、历史会话和任务依赖里，Agent 需要在多轮、多会话、持久工作区中尽早识别这些 hidden intents，而不是等用户逐条说明。
summary.importance: 这篇论文对预训练本身不是直接贡献，价值主要在 Agent eval 和 post-train 信号设计。它把“任务完成”与“减少用户负担”分开评估，这一点有用。很多长上下文或记忆能力评测只看是否能检索到历史信息，π-Bench 更关心检索到的信息是否被用来提前决策、减少澄清、保持跨会话一致性。对训练长周期助理来说，这类轨迹可以启发 SFT/RL 数据构造：奖励不只给最终文件是否正确，也要给早期意图识别、合理澄清和跨会话复用。
summary.technical_approach: Benchmark 构造为 5 个领域 persona：researcher、marketer、law trainee、pharmacist、financier。每个 persona 是一个 episode，包含 20 个 session，总计 100 个多轮任务。任务运行在持久项目环境中，Agent 通过工具、文件和工作区操作生成或修改具体 artifact，例如文档、结构化输出、代码或项目文件。每个 session 从自然但欠规格的请求开始，标注 hidden intents、跨任务依赖和跨会话可复用信息。评估维度包括 Proactivity 和 Completeness。Completeness 看工作流是否完成；Proactivity 看 Agent 是否足够早地发现、处理或澄清隐藏意图，并把历史偏好用于后续任务。这个设计区别于常规 memory benchmark：重点不是“记住了什么”，而是“何时、如何把记忆用于推进任务”。
summary.experiments: 论文在 9 个 frontier models 上做系统评测，结论是当前模型在任务完成和主动意图解决上都有明显缺口，并且二者不是同一能力。有些模型能完成显式任务，却没有提前处理隐藏约束，导致用户负担仍然较高；也有模型会频繁澄清，但不一定提升完成度。实验还显示，历史交互对后续 hidden intent resolution 有帮助，尤其是在命名规范、文件格式、偏好继承、跨 session artifact 修改这类场景。不同领域和任务类型之间差异较大，说明主动性不是单一长上下文能力可以覆盖的。
summary.reading_guide: 泛读即可，预计 20–30 分钟。优先看 Benchmark 设计部分和 Fig. 1，理解 session、episode、hidden intent、cross-session dependency 的组织方式。然后看评测指标定义，重点区分 Proactivity 与 Completeness。实验部分可以关注 9 个模型的能力差异、是否使用 prior interaction 的对照，以及失败案例。对预训练研究员而言，最值得看的不是排行榜，而是它如何把长程记忆、欠规格请求和可奖励轨迹连接起来。

summary_en.core_problem: π-Bench studies proactivity in long-horizon personal assistant agents. The user starts with an underspecified request, while the actual requirements are hidden in preferences, constraints, previous sessions, and task dependencies. The agent is expected to infer or clarify these hidden intents early enough to move the workflow forward.
summary_en.importance: The paper is not a direct contribution to pretraining, but it is useful for agent evaluation and post-training signal design. Its main value is the separation between task completion and user-burden reduction. Many memory benchmarks test whether an agent can retrieve prior facts. π-Bench asks whether the agent uses prior context at the right time to make decisions, maintain consistency, and avoid unnecessary user effort. This is relevant for building SFT or RL trajectories for long-horizon assistants, where rewards should cover early intent resolution and cross-session reuse, not only final artifact correctness.
summary_en.technical_approach: The benchmark contains 100 multi-turn tasks across five domain-specific personas: researcher, marketer, law trainee, pharmacist, and financier. Each persona forms one episode with 20 sessions. Sessions share a persistent project workspace, so files, intermediate artifacts, and previous decisions can affect later tasks. Each session begins with a natural but incomplete request. The benchmark annotates hidden intents, inter-task dependencies, and information that should persist across sessions. Evaluation has two axes: Completeness, which measures whether the workflow is finished, and Proactivity, which measures whether the agent identifies, resolves, or clarifies hidden intents early enough to support downstream decisions.
summary_en.experiments: The authors evaluate nine frontier models. The main finding is that current agents still struggle with both workflow completion and proactive intent resolution, and the two metrics capture different behavior. A model may complete explicit instructions while missing hidden preferences, or ask many clarifying questions without improving final outcomes. The experiments also show that prior interaction helps later intent resolution, especially for file conventions, formatting choices, user preferences, and artifact revisions across sessions. Performance varies substantially across domains and task types.
summary_en.reading_guide: A skim read is enough, about 20–30 minutes. Focus on the benchmark construction and Fig. 1 to understand how episodes, sessions, hidden intents, and cross-session dependencies are represented. Then read the metric definitions for Proactivity and Completeness. The experimental section is most useful for model behavior patterns and failure cases, rather than for the ranking itself. For pretraining-oriented readers, the interesting part is how the benchmark turns long-term memory and underspecified requests into trainable or rewardable trajectories.

recommendation.zh: Agent 评测里比较干净地抓住 hidden intent；看任务 schema 和 scoring，别把分数当模型能力全貌。
recommendation.en: A cleaner agent benchmark for hidden intent; read the task schema and scoring, but do not over-interpret leaderboard scores as full agent competence.

paper.title: TerminalWorld: Benchmarking Agents on Real-World Terminal Tasks
paper.abstract: We introduce TerminalWorld, a scalable data engine that automatically reverse-engineers high-fidelity evaluation tasks from "in-the-wild" terminal recordings. Processing 80,870 terminal recordings, the engine yields a full benchmark of 1,530 validated tasks, spanning 18 real-world categories, ranging from short everyday operations to workflows exceeding 50 steps, and covering 1,280 unique commands. From these, we curate a Verified subset of 200 representative, manually reviewed tasks. Comprehens

summary.core_problem: 如何构建一个“真实、可扩展、可复现”的终端（CLI）Agent评测体系：任务来自真实开发者终端录屏，而不是专家手写；同时要把录屏反向工程成可执行环境、可验证的测试与参考解，并尽量避免合成评测常见的伪任务与脆弱判分。
summary.importance: 这篇工作主要贡献在评测资产与评测生成流水线，而不是预训练方法本身。对基座研究的价值在于：它把“真实世界工具使用/交互式软件环境”的能力缺口量化出来，并提供了可持续扩展的数据引擎，后续可用于（1）更贴近真实分布的工具使用数据挖掘与持续预训练/中期训练；（2）把 agent 失败模式（探索摩擦、环境建模、测试脆弱性）转成可学习信号。它也给出一个重要警示：现有专家手写 CLI benchmark 与真实工作流的相关性很弱（文中给出 r=0.20），因此用它们做训练/选择模型可能会偏离真实需求。
summary.technical_approach:
TerminalWorld 的核心是把 asciinema 的“命令+输出”录屏转成标准化评测任务的三段式反向工程流水线。
1）意图与参考解蒸馏：录屏天然噪声大（typo、重试、冗长输出、无显式目标）。作者用 LLM 将整段 transcript 蒸馏成 outcome-oriented instruction（任务目标描述）与 clean command script（参考命令序列）。这里的关键不是生成“更难”的题，而是把人类真实操作压缩成可复现的最小充分步骤。
2）环境复现（Docker 镜像构建）：录屏不包含作者机器状态。作者用一个 LLM agent 在容器里“物理构建”环境：根据 transcript 推断依赖、安装软件、配置文件与数据；然后回放参考脚本，用运行时失败作为反馈迭代修复，重点是减少“幻觉依赖”（推断了但实际不需要/不正确的依赖）。这一步把任务从“文本描述”落到可执行系统状态。
3）测试生成与校准：录屏没有判分标准。作者不直接让 LLM 静态写 tests（容易 false positive/negative），而是让 agent 在已复现的容器里做 trial-based refinement：生成测试→执行→根据失败/可绕过情况迭代，直到测试既能通过参考解，又能较好排除投机路径。最终每个任务包含 instruction、可执行环境、参考解与测试套件。
产物层面：从 80,870 条录屏中自动化产出 1,530 个 validated tasks，并额外人工复核得到 Verified 200 子集。任务覆盖 18 类真实场景、1,280 个 unique commands，并强调与现有 Terminal-Bench 的命令覆盖差异（文中称 91% 命令不在 Terminal-Bench）。
summary.experiments:
评测对象包括 8 个前沿模型与 6 个终端 agent（文中举例 Claude Opus 4.7、GPT-5.5、Gemini 3.1 Pro；以及 Claude Code、Codex CLI、Gemini CLI 等）。在 TerminalWorld-Verified（200 题）上，最好的系统最高通过率为 62.5%，显示真实工作流仍有明显缺口。
作者还报告：
- “效率悖论（efficiency paradox）”：模型在真实环境里花更多计算做探索，但并不一定更接近解，失败往往表现为无效试探与上下文膨胀。
- agent 框架更多影响 cost-effectiveness，而不是能力上限：编排与工具链能省钱/省步数，但对能否解出任务的提升有限。
- 与 Terminal-Bench 的相关性弱：Terminal-Bench 分数对 TerminalWorld-Verified 的预测相关系数 Pearson r=0.20，提示现有手写题分布与真实任务分布差异大。
（注：给定你提供的全文片段，除 62.5%、1,530/200、80,870、1,280、91%、r=0.20 外，其它更细的分模型数字与消融细节未在片段中出现。）
summary.reading_guide:
泛读优先抓三块：
- 引言与方法总览：看清“录屏→任务”的三大难点与对应工程化解法（意图蒸馏、Docker 复现、测试校准）。
- 数据引擎细节：重点看环境复现的失败驱动修复机制，以及测试套件如何避免被 trivial bypass。
- 评测分析部分：关注 r=0.20 的相关性结论、失败模式归因（探索摩擦/无效试探），以及 Verified 子集的人工审计标准。
预计阅读时间：30–45 分钟可把方法与主要结论读清；若要复现/扩展数据引擎，需要进一步细读实现细节与任务格式定义。

summary_en.core_problem: How to build an authentic, scalable, and reproducible benchmark for terminal (CLI) agents by reverse-engineering real-world terminal recordings into executable tasks with reconstructed environments, reference solutions, and robust test suites—without drifting into hand-crafted puzzles or brittle auto-generated evaluation.
summary_en.importance: This is primarily an evaluation/data-engine contribution rather than a pretraining-method paper. Its relevance to foundation-model research is that it operationalizes “real terminal workflow competence” as a measurable target and exposes a distribution gap: expert-written CLI benchmarks correlate weakly with real workflows (Pearson r=0.20 reported). The pipeline can later serve as a source of realistic tool-use trajectories for continual pretraining/mid-training, and as a way to turn agent failure modes (exploration friction, environment modeling, test brittleness) into learnable signals.
summary_en.technical_approach:
TerminalWorld converts asciinema recordings (command + output transcripts) into executable evaluation tasks via a three-stage reverse-engineering pipeline.
1) Intent + reference script distillation: an LLM summarizes noisy transcripts (typos, retries, verbose outputs, no explicit goal) into an outcome-oriented instruction and a cleaned command script as the reference solution.
2) Environment reconstruction in Docker: since recordings omit machine state, an LLM agent iteratively builds a Docker image, replays the reference script, and uses runtime failures as feedback to infer missing dependencies/config/data while avoiding hallucinated requirements.
3) Test-suite generation with execution-grounded refinement: instead of static LLM-written tests, the agent runs a trial-based loop inside the reconstructed container to calibrate tests—ensuring the reference passes while reducing false positives/negatives and trivial bypasses.
Running this engine on 80,870 recordings yields 1,530 validated tasks; a manually audited Verified subset of 200 tasks is curated for rigorous benchmarking. The benchmark spans 18 categories and 1,280 unique commands, with 91% of commands claimed absent from Terminal-Bench.
summary_en.experiments:
Benchmarking on TerminalWorld-Verified (200 tasks) covers eight frontier LLMs and six terminal agents (examples listed: Claude Opus 4.7, GPT-5.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro; Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI). The best system reaches 62.5% pass rate, indicating substantial headroom on authentic workflows.
Key reported analyses include: an “efficiency paradox” where more exploration compute does not translate into progress; agent frameworks mainly shift cost-effectiveness rather than the capability ceiling; and weak predictiveness of Terminal-Bench for real-workflow performance (Pearson r=0.20).
(From the provided full-text excerpt, additional per-model numbers and ablations are not visible beyond these headline figures.)
summary_en.reading_guide: Skim with focus on: (1) the three practical challenges and their concrete solutions (distillation, Docker reconstruction, execution-grounded test refinement); (2) how the test calibration loop reduces brittle evaluation and bypasses; (3) the benchmarking analysis, especially the r=0.20 correlation claim and the failure-mode taxonomy around exploration inefficiency. 30–45 minutes is enough to understand the pipeline and main findings; deeper implementation details matter if you plan to reuse the data engine.

recommendation.zh: 这篇不改 pretrain recipe，但会改你对 agent eval 的 prior：现有终端 benchmark 相关性太低，先看数据引擎和 r=0.20 那个结果，再决定内部评测要不要重做。
recommendation.en: It won’t change your pretraining recipe, but it should change your prior on agent eval: current terminal benchmarks correlate too weakly; read the data engine and the r=0.20 result first.

paper.title: SaaSBench: Exploring the Boundaries of Coding Agents in Long-Horizon Enterprise SaaS Engineering
paper.abstract: As autonomous coding agents become capable of handling increasingly long-horizon tasks, they have gradually demonstrated the potential to complete end-to-end software development. Although existing benchmarks have recently evolved from localized code editing to from-scratch project generation, they remain confined to structurally simplified, single-stack applications. Consequently, they fail to capture the heterogeneous environments, full-stack orchestration, and system-level complexity of real

summary.core_problem: 构建一个更贴近真实企业级 SaaS 开发的长时程 coding agent 基准，用来测量从 PRD 理解、全栈实现、部署到调试的端到端能力，并解决现有基准在系统复杂度、市场真实度与评测机制上的不足。
summary.importance: 对预训练本身的直接信息增益有限，但它提供了更“长上下文 + 多语言/多框架 + 强交互”的评测压力源，可能反向影响代码预训练与后训练的数据配比（多语言、配置/脚本、DevOps 文本）、长上下文训练、以及 agentic tool-use 的训练信号设计。更适合作为 post-train/agent 评测资产，而不是预训练方法论文。
summary.technical_approach: SaaSBench 包含 30 个任务，覆盖 6 类 SaaS 域。每个任务提供长上下文 PRD、用于消歧的知识库、标准化运行环境，以及 DAG 形式的测试套件。评测采用 dependency-aware 的混合范式：用 DAG 表达前置依赖，通过 prerequisite gating 与 failure propagation control 把复杂系统的验证拆成可执行的线性检查链；同时提供 binary/weighted/LLM-as-judge 三种计分，覆盖部署可用性、数据建模、API 契约一致性、业务逻辑正确性、访问控制、工程质量等维度。
summary.experiments: 论文报告当前主流 coding agents 在该基准上仍有明显差距，暴露长时程规划与跨组件协同问题。当前提供的全文片段未包含各模型的具体分数表与对比数字，精确结论需以实验章节的主表为准。
summary.reading_guide: 泛读建议：优先看任务构建流程、DAG 评测设计与可执行验证节点的定义（理解它如何避免“只看最终是否跑通”的粗粒度信号）。再快速扫实验主表了解难点分布。预计 30–45 分钟可抓住要点。若关注预训练，只需记录它对数据与长上下文能力提出了哪些具体需求。

summary_en.core_problem: Introduce a realistic long-horizon benchmark for enterprise SaaS engineering to evaluate coding agents on end-to-end workflows (PRD understanding, full-stack implementation, deployment, iterative debugging) under heterogeneous stacks and system-level constraints.
summary_en.importance: Limited direct impact on pretraining methodology, but it is a strong evaluation pressure test that can feed back into pretrain/post-train decisions: multilingual/code+config+DevOps data mixtures, long-context training, and training signals for tool-using/agentic coding. Best viewed as an eval asset for coding agents rather than a pretraining paper.
summary_en.technical_approach: SaaSBench contains 30 tasks across 6 SaaS domains. Each task includes a long-context PRD, an ambiguity-resolution KB, a standardized runtime environment, and a DAG-based test suite. The evaluation is dependency-aware: prerequisite gating and failure-propagation control decompose complex system validation into executable checking chains. Scoring includes binary, weighted, and LLM-as-judge modes, covering deployment availability, data modeling, API contract consistency, business logic, access control, and engineering quality.
summary_en.experiments: The paper reports substantial gaps for current state-of-the-art coding agents on SaaSBench, especially in long-horizon planning and cross-component coordination. The provided excerpt does not include the detailed score tables; exact numbers should be taken from the main experiment section.
summary_en.reading_guide: Skim focus: benchmark construction pipeline, DAG evaluation design, and how executable validation nodes are defined to avoid overly coarse end-to-end signals. Then scan the main results table to see where failures concentrate. ~30–45 minutes to capture the essentials. If your focus is pretraining, extract the concrete capability demands implied by the tasks (context length, stack diversity, config/deployment artifacts).

recommendation.zh: 读 benchmark 构造和验证节点设计即可；它更像 agent eval 压力测试，不直接指导预训练数据配比。
recommendation.en: Read the benchmark construction and validation-node design; it is a useful agent-eval stress test, not a direct guide for pretraining data mixture.

paper.title: SpecBench: Measuring Reward Hacking in Long-Horizon Coding Agents
paper.abstract: As long-horizon coding agents produce more code than any developer can review, oversight collapses onto a single surface: the automated test suite. Reward hacking naturally arises in this setup, as the agent optimizes for passing tests while deviating from the users true goal. We study this reward hacking phenomenon by decompose software engineering tasks into three parts: (i) a natural language description of the specification (ii) visible validation tests that exercise specified features in is

summary.core_problem: 衡量长程 coding agent 在自动测试监督下的 reward hacking：模型是否只是学会通过可见测试，而没有真正满足用户规格。
summary.importance: 这不是 pretrain 论文，但它对 post-train 和 agent 评测有现实意义。贡献在于把 reward hacking 从泛泛讨论变成可操作的评测协议，用 visible tests 与 held-out compositional tests 的差距来量化。对基座研究员的价值主要在于理解训练信号质量和 verifier 漏洞。
summary.technical_approach: 提出 SpecBench。每个任务被拆成三部分：自然语言规格、可见验证测试、以及组合式 held-out 测试。作者假设如果 agent 真正理解规格，那么基于规格和可见测试写出的程序也应通过 held-out 测试；因此用两类测试通过率的 gap 作为 reward hacking 指标。这个设计把“骗过 reward”具体化为对可见测试的过拟合。
summary.experiments: 基准包含 30 个 systems-level programming tasks，覆盖从短程构建 shell 到更长程的系统编程任务。摘要没有给出参与评测的模型、agent 框架和具体 gap 数值，但从设计上看，最关键的是 held-out tests 是否确实只做组合泛化而不引入额外 specification shift。若这点做得干净，benchmark 才有诊断价值。
summary.authors_note: 作者机构为 Weco AI。给定信息中没有可确认的广为人知作者背景。

summary_en.core_problem: It measures reward hacking in long-horizon coding agents under automated-test supervision: are agents actually satisfying the user specification, or merely optimizing to pass visible tests?
summary_en.importance: This is not a pretraining paper, but it matters for post-training and agent evaluation. The contribution is to operationalize reward hacking with a concrete evaluation protocol, using the gap between visible tests and held-out compositional tests. For foundation-model researchers, the value is mainly in understanding training-signal quality and verifier loopholes.
summary_en.technical_approach: SpecBench decomposes each task into three parts: a natural-language specification, visible validation tests, and held-out tests that compose the same features in more realistic ways. The premise is that an agent that genuinely understands the specification should pass both suites; therefore, the pass-rate gap becomes a measure of reward hacking. This turns 'gaming the reward' into overfitting to visible tests.
summary_en.experiments: The benchmark contains 30 systems-level programming tasks, ranging from short-horizon shell-building tasks to longer-horizon systems programming settings. The abstract does not provide evaluated models, agent frameworks, or exact gap numbers. The main thing to inspect is whether the held-out tests truly measure compositional generalization rather than introducing a hidden specification shift; otherwise the benchmark becomes less diagnostic.
summary_en.authors_note: The paper is from Weco AI. The provided metadata does not identify any widely known authors with enough confidence for a stronger note.

recommendation.zh: 更像后训练/agent 评测资产，不是基座必读；知道有这么个“visible-vs-heldout gap”指标即可，除非你在做 coding RL 或 verifier 设计。
recommendation.en: This is more of a post-training/agent eval asset than a base-model paper; just remember the visible-vs-heldout gap metric unless you're actively working on coding RL or verifier design.

paper.title: MINTEval: Evaluating Memory under Multi-Target Interference in Long-Horizon Agent Systems
paper.abstract: Real-world agents operate over long and evolving horizons, where information is repeatedly updated and may interfere across memories, requiring accurate recall and aggregated reasoning over multiple pieces of information. However, existing benchmarks focus on static, independent recall and fail to capture these dynamic interactions between evolving memories. In this paper, we study how current memory-augmented agents perform in realistic, interference-heavy, long-horizon settings across diverse

summary.core_problem: 评测长程 agent 在多目标干扰、信息反复更新条件下的记忆能力，而不是只测静态、独立事实的召回。
summary.importance: 这是一个长程 memory benchmark。对基座预训练研究员的直接价值有限，但它提醒一个常被忽略的问题：真实 agent memory 不是简单 recall，而是会受到更新、冲突和跨片段聚合的干扰。贡献类型是 benchmark 设计，不是新模型。
summary.technical_approach: 提出 MINTEval，构造长且高度互联的上下文，其中信息会频繁更新并相互干扰。覆盖 state tracking、多轮对话、Wikipedia revisions、GitHub commits 等多域，并设计单目标召回、多目标聚合等问题类型，专门测 interference robustness。核心设计点是把 memory failure 从“忘了”细化为“被后续信息干扰”“跨目标聚合失败”等更接近真实系统的问题。
summary.experiments: 摘要没有给出具体模型或 agent 名单，但 benchmark 的诊断维度比较清楚：长上下文、动态更新、跨域泛化、不同问答类型。若要快速判断价值，主要看作者是否把干扰强度、更新频率和问题类型控制得足够干净，以及 baseline 是否覆盖 retrieval-based 与 summarization-based memory agent。
summary.authors_note: 作者来自 University of Texas at Austin。Mohit Bansal 是较知名的 NLP/VLM 研究者，长期做语言理解、推理与多模态。

summary_en.core_problem: It evaluates memory in long-horizon agents under multi-target interference and repeated information updates, rather than only testing static recall of independent facts.
summary_en.importance: This is a long-horizon memory benchmark. Its direct value to pretraining researchers is limited, but it highlights an often-missed issue: real agent memory is not simple recall, but recall under updates, conflicts, and cross-fragment aggregation. The contribution is benchmark design, not a new model.
summary_en.technical_approach: MINTEval builds long, highly interconnected contexts where information is frequently updated and interferes across memories. It spans multiple domains, including state tracking, multi-turn dialogue, Wikipedia revisions, and GitHub commits, and includes question types for single-target recall and multi-target aggregation. The key design choice is to decompose memory failure into more realistic modes such as interference from later updates and failure to aggregate across targets.
summary_en.experiments: The abstract does not list specific models or agents, but the diagnostic dimensions are clear: long contexts, dynamic updates, domain generalization, and diverse question types. To judge whether the benchmark is worth using, the main things to inspect are whether interference strength, update frequency, and question types are cleanly controlled, and whether the baselines cover both retrieval-based and summarization-based memory agents.
summary_en.authors_note: The authors are from the University of Texas at Austin. Mohit Bansal is a well-known NLP/VLM researcher with sustained work on language understanding, reasoning, and multimodal systems.

recommendation.zh: 知道这个 benchmark 在测“干扰下记忆”就够了；除非你正做 long-horizon agent memory，否则不值得花正文时间。
recommendation.en: It is enough to know that this benchmark targets memory under interference; unless you're actively building long-horizon agent memory systems, it does not deserve full-paper time.

institutions: The University of Texas at Austin

paper.title: RoadmapBench: Evaluating Long-Horizon Agentic Software Development Across Version Upgrades
paper.abstract: Coding agents are increasingly deployed in real software development, where a single version iteration requires months of coordinated work across many files. However, most existing benchmarks focus predominantly on single-issue bug fixes from Python repositories, with coarse pass/fail evaluation outcomes, and thus fail to capture long-horizon, multi-target development at real engineering scale. To address this gap, we present RoadmapBench, a benchmark of 115 long-horizon coding tasks grounded in

summary.core_problem: 解决现有 coding agent benchmark 过于短程、单问题、单语言、评价粗糙的问题，无法反映真实软件版本升级中的长周期开发能力。
summary.importance: 这是 benchmark 贡献。对预训练研究员的直接价值不在 agent 方法，而在它把“仓库级长期软件演化”作为更接近真实分布的评测对象，能反向暴露当前模型在长上下文、规划、代码编辑和状态跟踪上的能力边界。
summary.technical_approach: 提出 RoadmapBench：基于真实开源仓库版本升级构造 115 个长程任务，覆盖 17 个仓库、5 种编程语言。每个任务从 source-version 代码快照出发，给 agent 一个多目标 roadmap instruction，要求实现 target version 中引入的功能。任务粒度远大于常见单 bug fix，且评价不再只是简单 pass/fail，而是面向多目标升级场景的系统评测。
summary.experiments: 作者评测了 13 个前沿模型。任务中位修改规模为 3,700 行、51 个文件，明显高于 SWE-bench 一类短程修复设定。结果显示最强模型 Claude-Opus-4.7 仅解决 39.1% 任务，最弱模型更低，说明当前 coding agent 在真实长程开发上仍远未成熟。摘要未给出全部 baseline 名单和细粒度指标，但 benchmark 难度和失败率本身已经有信息量。
summary.authors_note: 作者来自北京大学、复旦大学、香港大学、清华大学等。给定信息中未出现可明确标注为业界广为人知的基础模型作者。

summary_en.core_problem: It addresses the gap that existing coding-agent benchmarks are too short-horizon, single-issue, Python-heavy, and coarsely evaluated to reflect real software version upgrades.
summary_en.importance: This is primarily a benchmark contribution. Its value to a pretraining researcher is indirect but real: it turns repository-scale software evolution into an evaluation target, exposing current limits in long-context reasoning, planning, code editing, and state tracking.
summary_en.technical_approach: The paper introduces RoadmapBench, a benchmark of 115 long-horizon tasks derived from real open-source version upgrades across 17 repositories and 5 programming languages. Each task starts from a source-version snapshot and gives the agent a multi-target roadmap instruction to implement functionality from the target version. The setup is much larger than standard single-bug-fix benchmarks and aims to evaluate realistic multi-file, multi-goal development.
summary_en.experiments: The authors evaluate 13 frontier models. The median task requires modifying 3,700 lines across 51 files, far beyond typical SWE-bench-style settings. Even the best model, Claude-Opus-4.7, solves only 39.1% of tasks, indicating that current coding agents remain weak on realistic long-horizon development. The abstract does not expose the full metric suite or all baselines, but the task scale and low success rates are already informative.
summary_en.authors_note: The authors are from Peking University, Fudan University, The University of Hong Kong, Tsinghua University, and others. No widely recognized foundation-model author can be confidently identified from the provided metadata.

recommendation.zh: 不是 pretrain 论文，但 benchmark 设得比 SWE-bench 更接近真实分布；看任务规模和失败案例就够，能帮助你校准“代码能力提升”到底来自哪一层。
recommendation.en: Not a pretraining paper, but the benchmark is closer to real software evolution than SWE-bench; read the task scale and failure analysis to recalibrate what current 'coding gains' actually mean.

paper.title: RecMem: Recurrence-based Memory Consolidation for Efficient and Effective Long-Running LLM Agents
paper.abstract: Memory systems often organize user-agent interactions as retrievable external memory and are crucial for long-running agents by overcoming the limited context windows of LLMs. However, existing memory systems invoke LLMs to process every incoming interaction for memory extraction, and such an eager memory consolidation scheme leads to substantial token consumption. To tackle this problem, we propose RecMem by rethinking when memory consolidation should be conducted. RecMem stores incoming intera

summary.core_problem: 长时运行的 LLM agent 需要外部记忆来突破上下文窗口，但现有记忆系统普遍对每次交互都做“急切式”LLM 记忆抽取与合并，导致构建阶段 token 成本过高。论文要解决的是：在不显著损失可用性的前提下，如何决定“什么时候值得调用 LLM 做记忆巩固”。
summary.importance:
更偏 agent 系统与成本工程，不是预训练方法论文。对基座研究的启发主要在两点：
1) 把“记忆写入”视为稀缺资源，采用事件触发（recurrence）而非逐步写入，类似把训练信号做门控；这类门控思想在持续学习/在线学习里也常见。
2) 反映了一个现实约束：很多 agent 方案的 token 成本主要消耗在“写记忆”而非“用记忆”，这会影响后续用交互轨迹做 continual pretrain / RL 数据闭环时的采样与记录策略。
summary.technical_approach:
RecMem 提出三层记忆架构与“基于复现的巩固”策略：
- Subconscious memory：对每条原始交互只做轻量 embedding 编码与存储，用于低成本检索与聚类，不调用 LLM。
- Consolidation trigger：当新交互在 subconscious 层检索到足够多语义相近/相关的历史交互（形成语义簇、出现持续复现）时，才调用 LLM 对该簇做记忆巩固，抽取 episodic memory（事件级摘要）与 semantic memory（更稳定的事实）。
- Semantic refinement：针对 episodic 摘要可能遗漏细粒度但对问答关键的信息，回看与该 episodic 关联的原始交互，补抽“持久且缺失”的事实并蒸馏为 semantic memory，降低信息损失。
整体上用“先廉价缓存 + 复现触发写入 + 写入后再精炼”替代“每步都写入”。
summary.experiments:
评测在两个长程记忆 benchmark：LoCoMo 与 LongMemEval-S；对比 Mem0、A-Mem、MemoryOS 等记忆系统。结论是：RecMem 在两套数据上问答准确率高于对比方法，同时显著降低记忆构建 token 成本。
- 在 LoCoMo 上，构建阶段 token 消耗最高可比基线降低 7.8×（论文图 1(d)）。
- 查询阶段 token 成本与现有系统相近，因此长交互历史下端到端成本更低。
（当前给出的全文片段未包含更细的分项数值与消融表；若论文后文提供触发阈值、簇大小、refinement 开关等消融，建议结合阅读以判断收益来自“少调用 LLM”还是“refinement 提升质量”。）
summary.reading_guide:
泛读即可，预计 20-30 分钟：
- 先看 Figure 1（尤其 token cost 对比）把握动机与收益量级。
- 重点看 consolidation trigger 的判定规则（相似度度量、阈值、簇维护方式）以及 semantic refinement 的具体抽取提示与合并策略，这两处决定了系统是否稳健。
- 如果关心可迁移性：留意在不同 benchmark/不同交互分布下触发频率如何变化，以及是否会对“长尾但重要的一次性信息”造成漏记。

summary_en.core_problem: Long-running LLM agents rely on external memory to overcome limited context windows, but most existing systems perform eager LLM-based consolidation on every interaction, incurring large token costs. The paper asks when consolidation should happen, aiming to cut construction-time cost without sacrificing downstream QA usefulness.
summary_en.importance: Primarily an agent-memory systems paper rather than pretraining research. The transferable insight for foundation-model work is the gating principle: treat memory writing (and, by analogy, expensive supervision/processing) as a scarce resource and trigger it only under recurrence. It also highlights a practical bottleneck for continual-data loops: in many deployments, token spend is dominated by memory construction, which affects what interaction traces are feasible to log, distill, or reuse for continual pretraining/RL.
summary_en.technical_approach:
RecMem introduces recurrence-based consolidation with a three-tier design:
- A “subconscious” layer stores raw interactions encoded by lightweight embedding models for cheap retrieval, avoiding LLM calls.
- Consolidation is triggered only when an incoming interaction finds enough semantically similar/related past interactions (forming a meaningful cluster). Then an LLM extracts episodic memories (event-level summaries) and semantic memories (more stable facts) from the cluster.
- A semantic refinement step revisits the raw interactions linked to each episodic memory to recover fine-grained but query-critical details that episodic summarization may omit, distilling them into semantic memory to reduce lossy compression.
Overall, it replaces per-turn eager extraction with “cheap buffering + recurrence-triggered write + post-write refinement.”
summary_en.experiments:
Evaluated on LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S, compared against Mem0, A-Mem, and MemoryOS. RecMem reports higher QA accuracy on both benchmarks while substantially reducing memory construction token cost.
- On LoCoMo, construction-time token consumption is reduced by up to 7.8× (as referenced around Fig. 1(d)).
- Query-time token cost remains comparable to baselines, so savings translate to lower end-to-end cost over long histories.
(The provided full-text excerpt does not include detailed ablations; if the paper contains them, the key is to separate gains from reduced consolidation frequency vs. refinement quality improvements.)
summary_en.reading_guide:
Skim-level read, ~20–30 minutes.
- Start with the cost breakdown figure(s) to understand where savings come from.
- Focus on the consolidation trigger mechanics (similarity metric, thresholds, cluster maintenance) and the semantic refinement procedure (what is extracted, how it is merged).
- Check robustness discussions: how often consolidation triggers under different interaction distributions, and whether one-off but important facts risk being missed.

recommendation.zh: 这不是 pretrain 论文，但它把“记忆提炼触发条件”从每步调用改成 recurrence 触发，系统味道很对；只看方法和成本曲线，别把任务收益当成普适结论。
recommendation.en: Not a pretraining paper, but the shift from eager memory extraction to recurrence-triggered consolidation is a clean systems idea; read the method and cost curves, not the task gains as universal truth.
